high_level_objective: Determine whether a context-graph-driven, outcome-adaptive LLM agent can design and conduct more scientifically valid long-horizon R&D than information-matched alternatives.
decision_question: What is the minimum currently identifiable and executable empirical unit for evaluating autonomous R&D?

requirements: Measures agent research behavior under at least two matched conditions.
Uses hidden or externally anchored evaluation evidence.
Requires no DeepVoice access and no unauthorized native runtime construction.
Can preserve identical model, task, feedback, target-evaluation, inference, and time budgets apart from declared treatment differences.

end_to_end_three_arm: not currently executable because full treatment is unimplemented
bundles search, graph state, evidence protocol, and held-out promotion
deterministic_protocol_mutation_only: tests validator correctness rather than autonomous research behavior

candidates.rationale: Highest thesis relevance but low identifiability and infeasible while the full treatment is unimplemented.
Separates retrieval from structured research state and is compatible with hidden-paper experimental-design tasks.
Strong direct analogue for later artifact optimization, but published costs and infrastructure make it a second-stage study.
Feasible process demonstration but lacks causal comparison and independent evaluation.
Useful prerequisite instrument test, not a sufficient autonomous-research efficacy study.

selection_rationale: SCOPE supplies direct counterevidence that naive search is not a monotonic treatment benefit.
The 2x2 design estimates the main effect of structured research state, the main effect of retrieval, and their interaction instead of bundling them.
ResearchClawBench demonstrates a public hidden-target task/rubric packaging pattern, though its final-report focus requires process metrics.
Arbor and HEP motivate explicit hypothesis/evidence state; Arbor shows structure without propagated insight is insufficient, and HEP shows self-validation must be replaced or audited.
Agent-Orchestrated Adaptive RAG supplies a direct mixed-effect retrieval-structure comparator, closing the H-B indirect-comparator gap.
Routing full reads show task-, budget-, verifier-, workflow-, and backbone-dependent effects; routing remains a separate deferred study rather than a Study A confound.

structured_research_protocol.on: stage-isolated configuration, protocol, and reporting with typed decision/evidence graph, mandatory rationale, alternatives, falsifiers, and update lineage

dynamic_retrieval.on: adaptive literature and method retrieval within the same total tool/inference budget

hypotheses.statement: Structured research state increases fatal-error-free experimental-design completion and improves low-level dataset, baseline, and metric configuration under matched budgets.
hypotheses.falsifier: No positive C10/C11 versus C00/C01 contrast, or any apparent gain disappears under condition-blind independent scoring.

hypotheses.statement: Dynamic retrieval has no assumed positive main effect; its effect may be null or negative when used without stage isolation.
hypotheses.falsifier: C01 consistently improves both high- and low-level design without raising redline errors under independent scoring.

hypotheses.statement: The structure-by-retrieval interaction is positive: retrieval contributes more when evidence acquisition is separated from protocol construction and recorded in the graph.
hypotheses.falsifier: The C11-C10 contrast is no larger than C01-C00, or added retrieval only increases citation count without changing a valid design decision.

primary_endpoint.name: fatal-error-free complete design
primary_endpoint.definition: A condition-blind plan passes all high-level main/ablation/analysis requirements and low-level dataset/baseline/metric requirements with no fabricated resource, incompatible metric, constraint violation, or post-outcome change.

secondary_endpoints: fraction of retrievals that change a hypothesis, control, resource, metric, or stopping rule
tokens, tool calls, wall time, and human intervention
selected_design.task_strategy: Use hidden-target, paper-derived dry-lab tasks through an evaluator-owned release boundary. Pilot tasks estimate variance and instrumentation failure only; pilot tasks never enter confirmation.
evaluation_strategy: Programmatic checks for resource existence, metric compatibility, required fields, and forbidden leakage where possible.
LLM rubric scoring is secondary to deterministic redlines and must be calibrated against an independent human-reviewed subset.
The root research agent never receives target papers or evaluation rubrics during treatment execution.
budget_invariants: only declared factor differences are allowed
selected_design.pilot_stop_rule: Do not launch confirmation until all four conditions complete on the predeclared pilot set, leakage tests pass, deterministic checks agree with manual review, and the evaluator yields an estimable paired variance. Two consecutive infrastructure-only failures stop the pilot for repair; they do not update H-A through H-C.
selected_design.follow_on_study: After Study A identifies a viable research-state treatment: (1) test flat queue versus tree versus tree-plus-insight with a held-out gate; (2) separately test fixed model versus calibrated query/role/depth-conditioned model–workflow routing under matched quality–cost budgets.

evidence_basis.role: direct experiment-design benchmark, search counterevidence, structured-workflow ablation
hidden-target task/rubric design and report-scoring limitations
tree/insight ablation, matched budgets, held-out admission, and scope limits
trajectory retrieval/utilization and evidence-gain stopping metrics
explicit hypothesis-evidence state and evaluator-independence requirement
unified routing formulation, common quality–cost protocol, task/budget nondominance
budget-aware resample/reroute and verifier-gated routing limits
controlled model–workflow orchestration trade-offs and difficulty counterevidence
calibrated subtask allocation, cost control, and distribution-shift limits
agent communication taxonomy and layered MCP/A2A trade-offs
human-agent collaboration grammar, authority, audit, and empirical boundary
intent-aware retrieval, semantic chunk repair, and locality limitation
compute-aware scientific retrieval and domain-reranker negative evidence
direct mixed retrieval-structure effects and cost/validity limits

dynamic_update_policy.positive: Search for replications, transfer limits, alternative mechanisms, and negative counterevidence; strengthen only the measured contrast.
dynamic_update_policy.null: Inspect power, rubric sensitivity, task heterogeneity, and whether structure helps only low-level configuration; do not declare the mechanism false.
dynamic_update_policy.negative: Search analogous cross-stage interference, graph overhead, anchoring, and utilization failures; narrow to the tested task/model/protocol.
dynamic_update_policy.execution_failure: Search implementation/specification evidence for the concrete failure; repair the same provisional node without updating scientific hypotheses.
dynamic_update_policy.retrieval_stopping: Stop a retrieval branch when new evidence does not change a hypothesis, method, control, resource, metric, or scope and independent support is sufficient.

current_blockers: Verify an evaluator-owned release boundary that excludes target papers and rubrics from treatment workspaces.
Select a pilot task subset without exposing hidden evidence to the root agent.
Provide an independent scoring route and human-calibration subset without self-attestation.
Create a separate fixed OpenResearch run contract for Study A; the current project command validates paper artifacts and cannot measure treatment outcomes.
Estimate compute/token cost before confirmation and preserve matched budgets.

feasibility_findings.finding: ResearchClawBench setup_workspace copies data and related_work but not target_study into the treatment workspace.
The pinned TaskRunner function launches a shell subprocess in the workspace with the inherited environment and does not itself create a filesystem sandbox.
feasibility_findings.implication: Prompt-level omission is not a sufficient hidden-evidence boundary; Study A needs a separate evaluator-owned filesystem or capability sandbox and a failing leakage test.

deferred_model_routing_study.question: Whether calibrated query-, role-, and recursion-depth-conditioned model–workflow routing improves the held-out quality–cost frontier without increasing fatal errors.
required_controls: same total inference and evaluation budget
logged candidate capabilities, availability, price, latency, decisions, and fallback
deferred_model_routing_study.deferral_rationale: Study A isolates structured state and retrieval with one fixed model. Routing would double the factorial and published evidence shows non-universal effects conditioned on task, budget, verifier, backbone, and workflow.

decision_changes: closed H-B direct retrieval-structure comparator gap
kept routing deferred from Study A
upgraded protocol and RAG design rationale

round8_decision_records.question: Should Study A move to an execution-graded research environment?
alternatives: keep design-only hidden paper-derived tasks
replace Study A with execution-graded closed-loop tasks
run both in the current cycle
round8_decision_records.rationale: Execution grading removes judge dependence, but the reviewed environment requires one GPU and about 24 hours per task in isolated containers, which the declared local resource ceiling cannot supply; running both would break matched budgets and exhaust the episode ceiling.
round8_decision_records.decision: Keep the design-only Study A. Execution-graded closed-loop evaluation stays deferred as Study C, now with a secured hosted-GPU execution path; it remains blocked on pre-registration rather than on access.
round8_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Preserves an executable current-cycle causal path; risk is that design-quality endpoints may not predict execution outcomes.
round8_decision_records.falsifier: If a design-score advantage fails to appear in any execution-graded replication, the design endpoint loses construct validity and Study A conclusions narrow to planning artifacts only.

required_before_launch: committed pre-registration with objective, fixed command, input digests, est_CU, stop rule, checkpoint plan
answered Q-0005 for the first GPU unit
cost ledger row opened before launch

round8_decision_records.question: Should retrieval conditioning become a separate Study A factor?
alternatives: add a fifth complexity-routed condition
treat conditioning as an inside-C11 mechanism with a secondary endpoint
ignore conditioning entirely
round8_decision_records.rationale: Complexity-conditioned routing is a positive precedent, and it explains why an unconditioned retrieval arm can be null or harmful; but adding a fifth arm breaks the 2x2 identification and the declared episode ceiling, and the reviewed classifier is trained from the same strategies it selects among.
round8_decision_records.decision: Keep four conditions. Log per-episode retrieval decisions and score retrieval-decision quality as a preregistered secondary endpoint inside the retrieval-on conditions.
round8_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Explains heterogeneity in the retrieval main effect without new arms; risk is that the secondary endpoint is underpowered and only descriptive.
round8_decision_records.falsifier: If retrieval-decision quality does not separate productive from unproductive episodes, the conditioning explanation for H-B heterogeneity is rejected.

round8_decision_records.question: What must the evaluator add before the pilot runs?
alternatives: keep deterministic redlines plus blinded rubric only
add integrity probes and failure attribution
defer both to confirmation
round8_decision_records.rationale: Open-ended long-horizon grading is gameable through grading-script edits, data leakage, and hardcoded metrics, and self-generated critique is not independent support; separating ideation from implementation failure requires a controlled disclosure condition rather than post-hoc reading of transcripts.
round8_decision_records.decision: Add fail-closed integrity probes to the evaluator gate and add an ideation-versus-implementation attribution arm to the instrument pilot by disclosing the withheld target idea without resources on a fixed task subset.
round8_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Makes scores harder to game and localizes failures; risk is added pilot cost and a disclosure condition that leaks target information if the subset is later reused.
round8_decision_records.falsifier: If integrity probes never fire on deliberately corrupted fixtures, the gate is decorative and must be redesigned.

required_resources.repositories: source-paper repositories with execution-based grading scripts

round9_decision_records.question: How do we know the structured research state was actually used in condition C10/C11?
alternatives: assume delivery equals use
ask the agent to self-report use
instrument a manipulation probe on the delivered artifact
round9_decision_records.rationale: A comparable ablation of persistent external context reported a null and could only interpret it because a manipulation probe showed the artifact was consumed; without that probe a null confounds "state does not help" with "state was never read". Self-report is not independent.
round9_decision_records.decision: Add a manipulation probe: a unique unguessable token is embedded in the structured state and the scored artifact must reference the state field carrying it; episodes failing the probe are quarantined before scoring, not silently averaged.
round9_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Makes a null H-A interpretable; risk is that the probe itself cues the agent to reference state superficially, so the probe checks reference to a decision-relevant field rather than the token string.
round9_decision_records.falsifier: If probe-passing and probe-failing episodes show the same score distribution, the probe measures compliance rather than use and must be redesigned.

round9_decision_records.question: How should a null structured-state result be reported given the 192-episode ceiling?
alternatives: report the null as "no effect"
report the null as underpowered and uninformative
pre-register an equivalence margin and test it
round9_decision_records.rationale: Null-hypothesis tests cannot establish absence, published paired comparisons frequently fail a resolution target, and underpowered designs are the norm in this literature; declaring "no effect" without a margin would be unsupported and declaring nothing wastes the block.
round9_decision_records.decision: Pre-register an equivalence margin on the continuous design score and test it with TOST on a task-clustered bootstrap; report the resolution target alongside every pairwise contrast and mark any contrast that cannot meet it as unresolved rather than null.
round9_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Turns an expected null into a bounded claim; risk is that the chosen margin is too wide to be scientifically meaningful, so the margin is fixed before any score is seen and justified against the redline definition.
round9_decision_records.falsifier: If the pre-registered margin exceeds the smallest score difference that changes a redline classification, the margin is meaningless and must be tightened.

round9_decision_records.question: What must the condition-blind judge demonstrate before its scores are admitted?
alternatives: agreement with a human subset only
agreement plus severity and halo diagnostics
replace the judge with deterministic checks alone
round9_decision_records.rationale: Judges with equal human agreement can differ greatly in severity, repeated calls make a biased score stable rather than valid, single-call sub-scores share a halo, and outcome-only judging misses failures that are silent in the artifact; deterministic checks alone cannot score open-ended design quality.
round9_decision_records.decision: Admit judge scores only after a calibration run on a human-anchored subset reports agreement, severity relative to the human anchor, and halo across dimensions; score each dimension in a separate call; add a step-level review pass for silent failures; use replication for stability and the human anchor for validity.
round9_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Separates rater bias from treatment effect; risk is added scoring cost and a smaller human anchor than ideal.
round9_decision_records.falsifier: If severity drift between judge versions exceeds the pre-registered equivalence margin, judge scores are inadmissible for cross-version comparison.

round9_decision_records.question: Should the two-repeat allocation change?
alternatives: increase repeats per task
decrease repeats and add tasks
keep two repeats and decompose variance
round9_decision_records.rationale: Repeat allocation should follow measured variance shares rather than convention, but no local variance components exist yet, so any change now would be arbitrary; the pilot is the instrument that produces those shares.
round9_decision_records.decision: No change. Keep two repeats, and pre-register a crossed random-effects decomposition of episode variance into task, condition, repeat, and residual so the confirmatory allocation is chosen from measured intraclass shares.
round9_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Preserves the current ceiling while making the next allocation evidence-based; risk is that the pilot is too small to estimate components precisely, which is recorded as a known limit.
round9_decision_records.falsifier: If task variance dominates residual variance, adding repeats cannot buy resolution and the design must add tasks instead.
round9_decision_records.falsifier_outcome: Falsifier resolved by measurement in the opposite direction: task variance was 0.0 percent and repeat residual 64.3 percent, so the no-change decision no longer holds.

round10_decision_records.question: Does the manipulation probe measure use of the structured state, or only compliance?
alternatives: keep verbatim field-name echo in the deliverable
drop the probe
respecify as filled-field consumption plus a carry-through signal
round10_decision_records.rationale: In the executed pilot all 8 structured episodes filled the scaffold while 7 of 8 never echoed the field name, so the probe fired on episodes whose state was demonstrably consumed. That is the failure this decision record predicted in its own falsifier: the probe measured verbatim compliance, not use.
round10_decision_records.decision: Respecify the probe: consumption is evidenced by a filled required field in the state artifact; carry-through of that field value into the design is reported as a separate weak signal; verbatim echo is retained only as a diagnostic and never quarantines an episode.
round10_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A null structured-state result stays interpretable without discarding valid episodes; risk is that a filled field is itself shallow compliance, which the carry-through ratio is meant to expose.
round10_decision_records.falsifier: If carry-through ratio is uncorrelated with any scored dimension across the confirmatory block, the respecified probe is also compliance-only and the structured-state factor cannot be verified.

evidence.observed: scaffold filled 8/8, verbatim echo 1/8, respecified consumption 5/8

round10_decision_records.question: The deterministic layer fired on no real artifact. Is it fit for the primary validity endpoint?
alternatives: keep fabrication redlines only and let the rubric judge carry discrimination
abandon the deterministic layer
add structural-completeness checks
round10_decision_records.rationale: Fabrication redlines fired on 0 of 16 executed artifacts while firing on every corrupted fixture, so they are correct but insensitive against competent output; leaving discrimination to an uncalibrated judge would concentrate the endpoint on the least independent layer.
round10_decision_records.decision: Add five deterministic structural-completeness checks covering ablation, uncertainty method, concrete named resources, a declared primary outcome, and a stopping rule or falsifier. They flag 13 of 16 pilot artifacts. Freeze them before confirmation.
round10_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Restores deterministic discrimination for the validity endpoint; the risk is severe and explicit: these checks were specified after observing pilot artifacts, so the pilot tasks become development data and the checks must be re-validated on unseen tasks.
round10_decision_records.falsifier: If the frozen checks flag every unseen confirmatory artifact or none of them, they carry no information and the validity endpoint must return to rubric scoring with an independent anchor.

round10_decision_records.question: Which model backend executes Study A episodes?
alternatives: the session provider
a hosted alternative provider
a self-hosted open-weights selector
a CPU compute instance
round10_decision_records.rationale: A live probe of four candidates returned: the session provider at HTTP 429 with its usage limit reached and a multi-day reset; one hosted provider timed out at 240 s; one router returned HTTP 402 for insufficient credits; two selectors answered correctly. Scaffold and orchestration studies both show effects are backbone-conditioned, so the backbone must be pinned and reported rather than treated as interchangeable.
round10_decision_records.decision: Pin the treatment backend to a single available selector for all conditions and reserve a different provider family for rubric judging, so judge and treatment do not share a blind spot. Record the probe outcome and the pin in the cost ledger.
round10_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Removes provider variation from the contrast and keeps the judge family separate; the cost is that all Study A conclusions are conditioned on one backbone and cannot be generalized.
round10_decision_records.falsifier: If the pinned selector becomes unavailable mid-block, the block is invalidated rather than silently completed on a substitute.

probe.openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol: HTTP 429 usage limit reached, resets in about 4.8 days

round11_decision_records.question: What supplies the scoring anchor when no human-rated set exists?
alternatives: wait for a human-rated set before scoring anything
accept uncalibrated judge scores
anchor on the withheld target design of the source study and score analytically
round11_decision_records.rationale: Criteria can be extracted from an expert reference rather than invented, direct artifact comparison invites hallucination so a checklist is the safer form, and analytic criteria scored separately avoid the halo of a single holistic call. Each pilot task already has a withheld expert design held by the evaluator.
round11_decision_records.decision: Adopt reference-anchored analytic coverage as the primary deterministic score: per task, an evaluator-owned element checklist derived from the withheld target design, each element scored separately, reported as covered elements and the missed set.
round11_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Gives a graded, discriminating deterministic score without any human rating; measured range on pilot artifacts is 0.667 to 1.000 where fabrication redlines gave 0 of 16. Risk: cue-based matching can reward vocabulary rather than substance.
round11_decision_records.falsifier: If coverage does not separate artifacts that an independent reader ranks differently, it measures vocabulary and must be replaced by judged element verdicts.
round11_decision_records.falsifier_outcome: Its own falsifier fired: adversarial probes show 0.969 false positives and 0.909 misses, so coverage measured vocabulary. Superseded by RD-2026-09-02-14A.

round11_decision_records.question: How is judge error bounded when the judge is admitted at all?
alternatives: agreement statistics only
always-answer judge with post-hoc error reporting
selective evaluation with calibrated abstention
round11_decision_records.rationale: Agreement alone does not bound error on any single verdict; selective evaluation calibrates a confidence threshold on a labelled set so the error rate among non-abstained verdicts is bounded at a stated risk level with stated confidence, and abstained items escalate instead of being scored badly.
round11_decision_records.decision: Admit judge verdicts only through a selective evaluator that fails closed while uncalibrated, and that selects its threshold using an upper confidence bound on the error rate rather than the empirical rate.
round11_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Converts an unbounded judge into a bounded one with explicit coverage loss; risk is that coverage becomes small enough that the judge contributes little, which is preferable to unbounded error.
round11_decision_records.falsifier: If coverage at the declared risk level falls below the fraction of episodes needed to resolve the primary contrast, judge scoring is dropped from the primary endpoint.

evidence.implementation_defect_found: a first implementation thresholded on the empirical error rate and certified a threshold that a finite-sample bound rejects

round11_decision_records.question: How many human-anchored labels does the calibration set need?
alternatives: choose a round number
reuse the pilot set
derive the size from the declared risk and confidence levels
round11_decision_records.rationale: The size follows from the guarantee itself: the smallest flawless calibration set whose upper confidence bound on the error rate meets the risk level. Guessing a size would repeat the underpowered-by-default pattern that the reviewed meta-analysis documents.
round11_decision_records.decision: Fix the calibration size from the guarantee. At 95 percent confidence the computed minimum flawless set is 25 labels for a 10 percent risk level, 11 for 20 percent, and 52 for 5 percent. Adopt the 10 percent level and therefore a target of at least 25 human-anchored labels, collected on tasks disjoint from the burned pilot set.
round11_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Turns an open blocker into a countable requirement; risk is that any calibration error raises the requirement sharply, so the set must be clean rather than merely large.
round11_decision_records.falsifier: If a clean 25-label set still fails to certify because judge errors appear at high confidence, the judge is miscalibrated at the top of its confidence range and no threshold will rescue it.

evidence.method: one-sided binomial upper bound at delta 0.05

round12_decision_records.question: Which tasks carry the confirmatory block, and how are they kept unseen?
alternatives: reuse the pilot tasks with fresh runs
sample new tasks at random from the corpus
select four unseen sources by design axis and freeze anchors before any scoring
round12_decision_records.rationale: The pilot tasks are burned twice over: they were the development set for the structural checks and two are designated disclosure tasks. New tasks must therefore come from sources that are neither pilot targets nor present in any released evidence pack, or the withheld design would be readable from the workspace.
round12_decision_records.decision: Freeze four confirmation tasks on four unseen sources spanning structure-versus-insight ablation, attribution of improvement, instrument-change measurement, and budget and access control. Their element checklists are written and frozen before any artifact exists, and each released evidence pack excludes its own target source.
round12_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Gives a clean confirmatory set with anchors that cannot be tuned to observed artifacts; risk is that four tasks remain too few to resolve the primary contrast, which the resolution target will state explicitly rather than hide.
round12_decision_records.falsifier: If any confirmation artifact reproduces its withheld target wording, the source leaked and that task is void.

confirmation_tasks.blocked_on: 25-label human-anchored calibration set before any judged scoring

round13_decision_records.question: How should the confirmatory episode budget be split between tasks and repeats?
alternatives: keep two repeats per cell as previously pre-registered
increase repeats to average run noise
spend the budget on tasks and keep one repeat, with a small repeated subset for monitoring
round13_decision_records.rationale: A measured decomposition on 32 executed episodes puts the repeat-to-repeat residual at 64.3 percent of variance and the task component at 0.0 percent, a boundary estimate. This refutes the assumption behind the earlier no-change decision, whose falsifier was that task variance would dominate. At a fixed episode budget the standard error of a condition mean is (repeats x interaction variance + residual) divided by budget per condition, which increases monotonically with repeats, so repeats buy less than tasks.
round13_decision_records.decision: Reverse the earlier allocation. Allocate the confirmatory block to the maximum number of tasks at one repeat per cell, and retain a small repeated subset only to re-estimate the residual and detect flaky execution. Record that the earlier two-repeat plan is superseded rather than deleted.
round13_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: At the 192-episode ceiling this moves the projected paired minimum detectable effect from about 0.049 to about 0.045 while quadrupling task coverage. Risk: with one repeat a flaky episode is invisible within its own cell, which the monitoring subset exists to catch.
round13_decision_records.falsifier: If the monitoring subset shows residual variance far above this estimate, one repeat is unsafe and the allocation returns to repeats.
round13_decision_records.note: The algebra stands; the variance inputs came from an endpoint later shown invalid, so the numeric split is void until recomputed (RD-2026-09-02-14B).

round14_decision_records.question: Is cue-matching coverage a valid primary endpoint?
alternatives: keep cue matching and accept the noise
add a negation guard and keep matching
demote matching to a recall filter and verify each candidate
drop deterministic scoring entirely
round14_decision_records.rationale: An adversarial probe set built in the planted-shortcut style shows the scorer counts negated sentences that contain the cue at a rate of 0.969 and misses genuine paraphrases at 0.909. A negation guard drives false positives to 0.000 but pushes misses to 1.000, so the failure is not surface polish: matching cannot decide whether a requirement is satisfied.
round14_decision_records.decision: Reject cue matching as the primary endpoint. Demote it to a high-recall candidate filter, and make element satisfaction a verified judgement over the candidate span, admitted only through the selective evaluator. Recompute variance components on the verified endpoint before any allocation is fixed.
round14_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Restores construct validity and makes partial credit meaningful; the cost is that the primary endpoint now depends on the judge, so the 25-label calibration set moves from optional to blocking for scoring, and the earlier variance-based allocation is void until recomputed.
round14_decision_records.falsifier: If verified element judgements disagree with a blinded human label more often than the declared risk level even at maximum confidence, no deterministic or judged endpoint is admissible and the study reports process metrics only.

round14_decision_records.question: What happens to the allocation derived in the previous cycle?
alternatives: keep the allocation because the algebra is independent of the endpoint
void it and recompute
ignore the issue
round14_decision_records.rationale: The allocation algebra is sound, but its inputs were variance components of an endpoint now shown to be invalid, so the numeric split between tasks and repeats rests on a measurement of vocabulary rather than of design quality.
round14_decision_records.decision: Void the numeric allocation from RD-2026-09-02-13A while retaining its algebraic result, and recompute variance components on the verified endpoint before fixing the confirmatory split. The 32 executed episodes are retained and can be rescored, so no episode is wasted.
round14_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Prevents an allocation decision from resting on an invalid measurement; the cost is one more scoring pass over retained artifacts once verification exists.
round14_decision_records.falsifier: If verified-endpoint components reproduce the same ordering, the earlier split was accidentally right and can be restored with evidence.

evidence.retained: the fixed-budget algebra and the 32 retained artifacts

round15_decision_records.question: Does the verified endpoint behave differently from the falsified one on real artifacts?
alternatives: assume the falsification generalises from synthetic probes
assume the two endpoints agree in practice
measure both on the same retained artifacts
round15_decision_records.rationale: A synthetic probe set can overstate a failure. Running both scorers over the same 32 retained artifacts and 192 element judgements gives the honest comparison: they correlate at 0.043 with a mean absolute difference of 0.484, so the falsification holds outside the probe set and the endpoints are not interchangeable.
round15_decision_records.decision: Adopt filter-plus-verification as the endpoint of record and retain the element verdicts as the labelling material for calibration. Report the falsified endpoint only as a superseded measurement, never as a result.
round15_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The endpoint now reflects satisfaction rather than vocabulary; the cost is a judge dependency and 192 additional model calls per rescoring pass.
round15_decision_records.falsifier: If verified verdicts disagree with blinded human labels beyond the declared risk level at maximum confidence, no scored endpoint is admissible and the study reports process metrics only.

round15_decision_records.question: What is the allocation once variance is recomputed on the verified endpoint?
alternatives: restore the earlier one-repeat split
keep two repeats
choose the split on the recomputed components
round15_decision_records.rationale: On the verified endpoint the residual is 83.8 percent, the task component 16.2 percent, and both condition and interaction components are estimated at zero. With the interaction component at zero the standard error of a condition mean no longer depends on how the fixed budget is split between tasks and repeats, so resolution cannot be bought by reallocating.
round15_decision_records.decision: Fix the split on grounds other than resolution: allocate to the maximum number of tasks at one repeat to widen task coverage and expose task-level heterogeneity, and keep a repeated subset for residual monitoring. Record that the projected paired minimum detectable effect is about 0.081, roughly double the value the falsified endpoint suggested.
round15_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Honest sizing: the block resolves less than previously projected, which is a property of the endpoint rather than of the allocation. Risk: at this resolution the confirmatory block may be unable to separate conditions at all, which the resolution target will state before any score is read.
round15_decision_records.falsifier: If a zero interaction component is an artifact of the small block, a larger block will show a nonzero component and the allocation must be recomputed.

round16_decision_records.question: Is the verifier stable enough to be worth spending human labels on?
alternatives: collect labels immediately
abandon judged scoring
measure reliability first and set a confidence floor from it
round16_decision_records.rationale: Judge scores move when the evaluator changes and when the same query is merely repeated, so stability is part of the instrument. Measured on 64 stratified pairs: test-retest agreement 0.844, cross-model agreement 0.703, chance-corrected kappa 0.411. Both rise above 0.9 confidence, where retest agreement is 0.880, cross-model agreement 0.920, and none of the 20 high-confidence pairs disagreed across models.
round16_decision_records.decision: Adopt a reliability floor before calibration: verdicts below 0.9 confidence abstain by default, and the calibration threshold may only tighten that floor, never loosen it. Report reliability separately from validity and never present agreement as correctness.
round16_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Removes the noisiest verdicts before human labels are spent; the cost is reduced coverage, since roughly a third of judged pairs sit below the floor.
round16_decision_records.falsifier: If human labels show that above-floor verdicts are wrong at a rate exceeding the declared risk level, the floor is not protective and judged scoring is dropped.

round16_decision_records.question: How are the calibration items sampled?
alternatives: pure uncertainty sampling
random sampling
stratified sampling across confidence bands
round16_decision_records.rationale: Uncertainty sampling concentrates on the hardest items, which is also where annotation error concentrates, so a threshold certified on such a set would be calibrated on a harder population than the one it governs. Random sampling wastes labels on items the floor already excludes.
round16_decision_records.decision: Sample the calibration set stratified across confidence bands with task and condition spread and a recorded seed, and publish the blinded form separately from the evaluator-owned key.
round16_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The certified threshold governs the population it was drawn from; the cost is that the low-confidence band is thin in the retained pool, so the current form holds 22 of the target 25 items and must be topped up from new artifacts.
round16_decision_records.falsifier: If agreement differs sharply between strata after labelling, one threshold cannot serve all bands and the evaluator needs band-specific thresholds.

round17_decision_records.question: The public-name gate blocked the word "submission". Should the gate change?
alternatives: rename the thesis artifacts to avoid the word
disable the pattern
narrow the pattern to competition-specific forms and prove it still fires
round17_decision_records.rationale: The pattern was inherited to keep competition and test-instance fingerprints out of public text, but "submission" is ordinary vocabulary for a thesis that must be submitted, so the gate was blocking correct language rather than a leak. Disabling it would remove a real protection, and renaming artifacts would distort the thesis to fit a regex.
round17_decision_records.decision: Narrow the pattern to competition-specific forms (leaderboard, archive filenames, hackathon, submission limit or quota) and verify by fixture that it still fires on each competition term while staying silent on thesis submission wording. A gate change is itself an audited modification, not a silent edit.
round17_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The gate keeps its protective scope and stops producing false positives; the risk is that a future competition phrase not in the list slips through, which the fixture list must grow to cover.
round17_decision_records.falsifier: If any competition or instance identifier appears in public output while the narrowed gate stays silent, the narrowing was wrong and must be reverted.

round18_decision_records.question: Where do the Korean summary and keywords live, given a LaTeX toolchain with no CJK font?
alternatives: embed Hangul in the LaTeX source
keep them only in a side file
keep the source ASCII and inject them during the Word build
round18_decision_records.rationale: Embedding Hangul would break the deterministic PDF build, whose reproducibility is the evidence base for every claim in the thesis. Leaving them only in a side file would ship a submission artifact missing a required section. Injecting during the build keeps one source file for the text and one reproducible build for the evidence.
round18_decision_records.decision: Keep the manuscript source ASCII, keep the Korean summary and keywords in a single side file, and have the Word build inject them into the converted document, failing the build if the summary exceeds 500 characters or the keywords exceed five.
round18_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The submission artifact satisfies the official section and length limits while the deterministic PDF stays reproducible; the risk is drift between the two outputs, which the build receipt binds by hashing both sources.
round18_decision_records.falsifier: If the injected section is absent or over the limits in a rebuilt artifact, the build is not enforcing its own contract.

round18_decision_records.question: The Word artifact rendered no in-text citations. Accept or fix?
alternatives: accept and note the gap
add a bibliography processor and a separate bibliography database
materialise the numbering already enforced by the validator
round18_decision_records.rationale: The converter emitted citation elements with no numbers, which left dangling punctuation and violated the official requirement for bracketed citation numbers. A second bibliography database would create a duplicate source of truth for references that could silently diverge from the manuscript.
round18_decision_records.decision: Materialise the first-citation numbering that the validator already enforces, substituting bracketed numbers into a staged copy for the Word build only, leaving the manuscript source unchanged.
round18_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: 57 citations now render as bracketed numbers matching the reference list order; the risk is that the numbering diverges if the substitution and the validator disagree, which is why both derive from the same first-citation rule.
round18_decision_records.falsifier: If any rendered number does not match the position of its entry in the reference list, the substitution is wrong and must be regenerated.

round19_decision_records.question: Three official format properties were inherited from a reference document and never verified. Verify, or trust?
alternatives: trust the reference document
verify by opening the file in a word processor
verify from the artifact bytes and implement anything missing at build time
round19_decision_records.rationale: Inherited properties were assumed rather than checked, which is the same mistake that produced a locator set unverifiable outside one working tree. Parsing the artifact parts showed all three were absent: chapters carried no numerals, no line spacing was set, and there was no footer part at all. Opening the file by hand would prove one machine, not the artifact.
round19_decision_records.decision: Verify every official format property by parsing the artifact parts, and implement the missing ones in the committed builder so each rebuild reproduces them: Roman chapter numerals with front matter unnumbered, double spacing in document defaults, and a footer with a page field wired through the relationship and content-type parts.
round19_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The artifact now satisfies the checkable format requirements and each rebuild reasserts them; the risk is that a word processor may render a property differently from what the parts declare, which the unattended export could not confirm on this machine.
round19_decision_records.falsifier: If a rebuilt artifact lacks any of the three properties, or a word processor renders single spacing or no page number, the builder is not enforcing the format and the check must move into the validator.

round20_decision_records.question: The builder asserts the official format. What prevents a later rebuild from silently losing it?
alternatives: trust the builder
check the artifact by hand after each build
move the checks into the deterministic gate and prove they fail closed
round20_decision_records.rationale: A property asserted only by the producer is unguarded: the same builder that adds a footer can stop adding it, and nothing would notice. The project has already been bitten once by an artifact that satisfied its producer but not an independent checkout.
round20_decision_records.decision: Move the artifact format checks into the deterministic validator so that title, front matter, chapter numerals, summary length, keyword count, double spacing, page numbering, citation numbering, and forbidden names are all re-derived from the artifact bytes on every run, and prove the gate fires by mutating the artifact.
round20_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: A regression in the submission artifact now fails the same gate that guards the manuscript; the cost is that the gate encodes an expected reference count that must be updated when the bibliography grows.
round20_decision_records.falsifier: If a mutated artifact passes the gate, the check is decorative and must be rewritten.

round21_decision_records.question: Must the submission artifact be byte-reproducible, or is a correct-looking rebuild enough?
alternatives: accept content equivalence and stop pinning the artifact digest
pin the digest and rebuild only on one machine
make the build deterministic so any checkout reproduces the same bytes
round21_decision_records.rationale: A clean-clone rebuild produced a different digest, so the pinned receipt would have failed for anyone but this machine, which is the same defect that once made the locator set unverifiable elsewhere. Verification also requires more than determinism: an independent party must be able to recover the source state and instructions, which is why the builder is committed alongside the artifact.
round21_decision_records.decision: Make the build deterministic by pinning every packed entry timestamp and the document property timestamps to the epoch already used for the deterministic PDF, and write parts in sorted order. Keep the builder committed so the instructions travel with the artifact.
round21_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Any checkout now reproduces the artifact byte for byte, so the pinned digest is a real check rather than a machine-specific fact; the risk is that a converter upgrade changes output and breaks the digest, which is the intended signal rather than a failure.
round21_decision_records.falsifier: If two checkouts at the same commit produce different digests, the build is still not reproducible and the receipt cannot be trusted.

round22_decision_records.question: The thesis claims the loop corrects itself. What is the measured value of that claim?
alternatives: assert self-correction narratively
count only the falsified endpoint
census the whole decision record with committed code and report the rate with its limits
round22_decision_records.rationale: A claim about the process needs process measurement, and one source argues that evaluating a sequence of studies must consider order and method rather than a final pooled number. A census computed by committed code can be re-derived by a reader; a narrative assertion cannot. The same literature warns that operational rigor substitutes for understanding, so a rate must be reported with what it cannot show.
round22_decision_records.decision: Measure the decision record with a committed script and fixtures, and report that 3 of 27 recorded decisions were revised, every revision triggered by the project's own executed measurement, alongside the explicit statement that a single project without a comparison group cannot show the practice caused the revisions.
round22_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The self-correction claim becomes a re-derivable number instead of a narrative; the risk is that a reader mistakes a descriptive rate for evidence of effectiveness, which the recorded scope line addresses directly.
round22_decision_records.falsifier: If the census counts records the ledger does not contain, or misses revised decisions, the number is wrong and the claim must be withdrawn.

round23_decision_records.question: What cost quantity should the confirmatory block report per episode?
alternatives: wall-clock duration as a proxy
total tokens reported by the provider
dollar cost
marginal input plus output tokens with the fixed floor reported separately
round23_decision_records.rationale: Measurement replaced the proxy. Three probes on the pinned backend showed a fixed context floor of 46,763 tokens identical across probes, and dollar cost for identical work varying twelvefold with cache state, which is an artefact of execution order rather than a property of the condition. Reporting totals would put the condition contrast at about one percent of the measure. The literature independently warns that provider totals conceal different accounting and that augmentation gains vanish against a token-matched baseline.
round23_decision_records.decision: Report marginal input plus output tokens as the per-episode cost, report the fixed harness floor separately as a constant, and do not use dollar cost or wall-clock duration for any comparison between conditions.
round23_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Cost becomes attributable to the condition instead of to cache state and harness overhead; the risk is that marginal tokens omit cached context that still consumes provider capacity, which is why the floor is reported rather than discarded.
round23_decision_records.falsifier: If the fixed floor varies materially across episodes of the same backend, treating it as a constant is wrong and cost must be modelled per episode.

round24_decision_records.question: After the fixed-floor assumption failed on real episodes, what cost quantity is admissible?
alternatives: keep marginal tokens and a constant floor
report only total tokens
report context tokens and marginal tokens as two separate quantities
round24_decision_records.rationale: Replicating the probe measurement on real episodes falsified the previous decision one cycle after it was made. The probes ran in an empty directory and measured only harness context; a real episode also carries its mounted workspace, and the full condition mounts an evidence pack of 145,906 bytes. Context tokens differed by 24,900 between conditions and totals differed by a factor of 1.487, so the floor is not a constant and marginal tokens alone hide most of what a condition costs.
round24_decision_records.decision: Report context tokens and marginal tokens as two separate quantities per episode, treat neither as constant, and continue to exclude dollar cost from comparisons because it still varies with cache state.
round24_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Cost attribution now distinguishes what the condition puts into context from what the agent produced; the risk is that cache read and write are priced differently, so token counts and money remain separate reports rather than one number.
round24_decision_records.falsifier: If context tokens for the same condition and task vary widely across repeats, a per-episode report is still not enough and cost must be modelled with repeats.

round25_decision_records.question: Is a single episode enough to report the cost of a condition?
alternatives: report one episode per condition
report repeats only for the retrieval condition
report every cost quantity as a mean over repeats with its spread, and never as a single episode
round25_decision_records.rationale: The falsifier of the previous decision fired for one condition. With identical workspace digests within each condition, the minimal condition varied by 2.90 percent while the retrieval condition varied by 11.34 percent, and its within-condition range covers 61.1 percent of the between-condition gap. Agents are independently reported to show substantial run-to-run variance under identical inputs, so a single episode is a draw from a distribution rather than a value.
round25_decision_records.decision: Report every cost quantity as a mean over repeats with its observed spread, never as a single episode, and treat the retrieval condition as requiring more repeats than the minimal condition because its variance is roughly four times larger.
round25_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Cost comparisons carry their own uncertainty instead of implying precision that three episodes cannot support; the risk is that three repeats is itself a small sample, which is why the spread is reported rather than a confidence claim.
round25_decision_records.falsifier: If the spread of the retrieval condition does not shrink as repeats increase, the variance is not sampling noise but a property of the condition, and cost must be modelled as a distribution rather than summarised by a mean.

round26_decision_records.question: The cost instrument was wrong by an order of magnitude and its fixture protected the error. What must change?
alternatives: patch the parser and keep the reported numbers
patch the parser and re-run only the affected condition
void every number the instrument produced, fix the parser, capture complete transcripts, and re-measure from scratch
round26_decision_records.rationale: The parser summarised a run by its last usage record, but usage is per completed API call and context is re-sent on each call, understating one episode by 14.4 times. The fixture asserted the wrong behaviour, so the suite passed while the instrument was wrong: a fixture that encodes the author assumption tests the assumption, not the system. Two further defects surfaced during the fix, transcript truncation through standard output and a buffer that swallowed later records, the second caught by a failing-first fixture.
round26_decision_records.decision: Void every cost number the instrument produced across the three preceding cycles, sum usage over completed calls, write transcripts to files and report whether each is complete, and re-measure all six episodes before any cost figure is used again.
round26_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Cost figures now reflect billed calls rather than a final record, and truncation is visible instead of silent; the risk is that fixtures written by the same author can still encode a shared misunderstanding, which is why each fixture now asserts against transcript structure rather than against expected totals.
round26_decision_records.falsifier: If a transcript reports complete but its summed call count disagrees with the provider billing record, the aggregation is still wrong.

round27_decision_records.question: After one instrument was found wrong with a passing suite, are the other instrument suites adequate?
alternatives: read the suites and judge them
add more assertions where they look thin
mutate each module and keep only the fixtures that a surviving mutation forces
round27_decision_records.rationale: Reading is what missed the previous defect, so the suites were audited by injecting semantic faults and observing whether they failed. An oracle that draws its expected value from the system it judges cannot fail, which is precisely how the cost fixture protected a wrong parser, and a suite can hold high coverage while leaving a documented behaviour unvalidated.
round27_decision_records.decision: Audit every instrument by mutation, add fixtures only where a mutation survived, and record that three modules still have no paired suite rather than implying full coverage.
round27_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Four surviving mutations became four caught mutations, including one that neutralised the whole fail-closed admission gate; the risk is that passing a mutation set does not prove correctness, only that these specific faults are detected.
round27_decision_records.falsifier: If a mutation that changes a reported quantity survives the suite after this audit, the suite is still inadequate.

round28_decision_records.question: Three instrument modules had no test suite. What standard should new suites meet?
alternatives: write assertions that mirror the current output
write assertions and accept a passing suite as done
write assertions from the contract, then mutate the module and keep only what a surviving mutation forces
round28_decision_records.rationale: A suite written by the author of the code can restate the implementation instead of testing it, which had already happened once here. Expected values were therefore fixed from each module contract rather than read back from the module, and every new suite was audited by mutation before being accepted. For the judge module no reliable oracle exists, so the suite asserts the deterministic shell around the model through an injected runner.
round28_decision_records.decision: Give all three modules paired suites whose expected values come from the stated contract, audit each by mutation, and classify any surviving mutation as either a test gap to fix or an equivalent mutant to document.
round28_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Twenty of twenty-one injected faults were caught and the twenty-first was shown by execution to be an equivalent mutant; the risk is that a mutation set chosen by the same author can still miss a fault class neither the code nor the mutations consider.
round28_decision_records.falsifier: If a mutation that changes any reported quantity survives one of these suites, the suite is inadequate and the audit conclusion is wrong.

round29_decision_records.question: Every recorded score came from unaudited instrument code. Do the recorded results still hold?
alternatives: assume the audit changed nothing because no logic was modified
re-run the blocks from scratch
re-derive the deterministic quantities from the retained artifacts with the audited code and compare
round29_decision_records.rationale: An artifact that runs is not the same as a claim that can be reproduced, and replaying historical claims from a frozen collection commonly stops before the claim is reachable. Re-running would spend the frozen tasks and still not test the recorded numbers, so the recorded numbers were re-derived from the retained artifacts instead.
round29_decision_records.decision: Re-derive every deterministic recorded quantity from the retained artifacts with the audited instruments, report judged verdicts as outside the check because the judge is nondeterministic, and treat any mismatch as invalidating the recorded number.
round29_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: Both blocks re-derived exactly, so the deterministic parts of the recorded results are reproducible from committed bytes; the risk is that this says nothing about the judged endpoint, which is why the exclusion is stated in the receipt rather than implied.
round29_decision_records.falsifier: If any re-derived deterministic quantity differs from its recorded value, the recorded value is wrong and must be corrected before use.

round30_decision_records.question: The judged layer could not be re-derived deterministically. How reproducible is it?
alternatives: treat judged verdicts as fixed once recorded
re-run everything and replace the record
replay a stratified subset and report reproducibility per confidence band
round30_decision_records.rationale: Replaying 24 recorded judgements with the same judge and artifacts gave 18 of 24 overall, but the split by band is the result: 10 of 10 above 0.9 confidence, 8 of 10 between 0.7 and 0.9, and 0 of 4 below 0.7. Repeated calls can disagree because the judge is stochastic or because the item is ambiguous, and this design cannot separate those causes.
round30_decision_records.decision: Report judged reproducibility per confidence band rather than as one number, keep the 0.9 admission floor which the measurement supports directly, and record that verdicts below 0.7 carry no reproducible content and are not scored.
round30_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The admission floor is now supported by a replay measurement rather than by prior reasoning alone; the risk is that replay is not correctness, since no human label exists for any replayed item.
round30_decision_records.falsifier: If a larger replay sample shows the band above 0.9 disagreeing materially, the admission floor is not supported and must be raised or abandoned.

round31_decision_records.question: Are low-confidence items unlabelable, and should they leave the calibration set?
alternatives: drop the low-confidence items as undecidable
keep them and keep their recorded verdicts
keep the items but replace a recorded low-confidence verdict with a modal verdict over repeats
round31_decision_records.rationale: Repeating each low-confidence item five times gave a mean modal share of 0.88 with two items unanimous, so the items carry a stable answer and are labelable. The recorded draw is what fails: it matches the modal answer in only 1 of 5 cases and returned unclear three times where repeats converge on a definite verdict. Annotation variance can come from item ambiguity or from the rater, and this separates them for these items.
round31_decision_records.decision: Keep the three low-confidence items in the calibration set, replace any recorded low-confidence verdict with a modal verdict over at least five repeats before comparing it with a human label, and correct the earlier claim that verdicts below 0.7 carry no reproducible content.
round31_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The calibration set keeps the items that discriminate most, and the judge side of each comparison becomes a stable estimate rather than one draw; the risk is that agreement across repeats measures concentration of an answer distribution and not correctness, so a stable modal answer can still be wrong.
round31_decision_records.falsifier: If the modal verdict over more repeats moves for these items, five repeats is not enough to estimate it and the modal answer cannot be used either.

round32_decision_records.question: Does the modal recomputation rule also apply to the mid confidence band, and what does confidence predict?
alternatives: apply modal recomputation to every band
apply it only below 0.7 on the assumption that the mid band is fine
measure the mid band and scope the rule to what the measurement supports
round32_decision_records.rationale: Ten mid-band items over five repeats each gave a mean modal share of 0.86, close to the low band 0.88, so within-item stability does not separate the bands. What separates them is whether the recorded draw represents the item: 9 of 10 in the mid band against 1 of 5 in the low band. Reported confidence therefore predicts representativeness of a draw rather than concentration of the answer distribution.
round32_decision_records.decision: Keep modal recomputation scoped to verdicts below 0.7 confidence, apply it to the five low-band records and the five matching calibration key entries while retaining every original single draw, and record the counterevidence that majority aggregation can reduce accuracy on hard items as an unresolved risk rather than a settled one.
round32_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The record now matches the adopted rule and the unclear category disappears because all three unclear verdicts were low-confidence single draws; the risk, taken from published counterevidence, is that aggregating repeats on the hardest items can entrench a wrong answer, and only human labels can arbitrate that.
round32_decision_records.falsifier: If the human calibration labels agree with the original single draws more often than with the modal verdicts on these items, the correction made the record worse and must be reverted.

round33_decision_records.question: Do the verified endpoint numbers survive the verdict correction?
alternatives: assume four changed verdicts out of 192 cannot matter
recompute only the headline number
reproduce the recorded numbers first, then recompute everything on the corrected record and report both
round33_decision_records.rationale: A recomputation that has not first reproduced the original is not a check, so the pipeline was validated against the recorded numbers before the corrected record was used. That step immediately paid: the recomputed minimum detectable effect disagreed with the record, and deriving the quantity showed the record was right and the check was wrong by a factor of the square root of two.
round33_decision_records.decision: Report the recomputed endpoint on the corrected record beside the original, state that the task share rose from 16.2 to 21.5 percent while condition and interaction stay at zero, and note that no conclusion depends on the difference.
round33_decision_records.expected_effect_and_risk: The endpoint numbers now match the corrected record and the structural conclusion is unchanged; the risk is that four changed verdicts out of 192 is a small perturbation and this says nothing about how the endpoint would behave under a larger correction.
round33_decision_records.falsifier: If a recomputation on the corrected record cannot reproduce the recorded numbers when run on the original record, the recomputation is untrustworthy and neither set may be reported.
